source: Official JoSAA 2025 Opening & Closing Rank archive (josaa.admissions.nic.in, Year 2025, Round 6 = final round, Institute type IIT), scraped directly; every value cross-checked against the 'Opening-Closing Ranks' section of the official JEE (Advanced) 2025 Joint Implementation Committee report (jeeadv.ac.in/reports/2025.pdf), which matched for all entries.

adv_to_main.reasoning: No official body publishes paired Main/Advanced ranks (the JIC 2025 report maps Main application numbers to Advanced roll numbers but gives no Main ranks), and no systematic published analysis was found, so this is a MODELLED estimate anchored on official pool sizes and a few verified topper pairs. Definition used: the typical (median) JEE Main CRL rank of a student who obtains a given JEE Advanced CRL rank, i.e. roughly where the students admitted to an IIT branch sit on the Main scale. Official inputs (JIC 2025 report): 2.5 lakh shortlisted from Main, 1,87,223 registered, 1,80,422 appeared in both papers, 54,378 qualified. Model: Monte Carlo of ~14 lakh Main candidates; top 2.5 lakh by Main eligible; Advanced participation ~95% among the top 20k Main ranks falling to ~55% near the cutoff (~72% overall, matching the official 1.80/2.5 lakh); Main and Advanced scores share a common ability with correlation 0.90-0.93, calibrated so Advanced top-10 rankers mostly hold Main ranks in the tens to low hundreds, as observed (2025: Advanced AIR 2 Saksham Jindal was Main AIR 10; Advanced AIR 1 Rajit Gupta and AIR 16 Devdutta Majhi both scored 100 percentile in Main, i.e. Main top ~24). Simulated median Main/Advanced ratio: ~3-5 for Adv 50-200, ~2.3-3.3 for Adv 200-1000, ~2.0-2.6 for Adv 1000-3000, ~1.9-2.2 for Adv 3000-7000, ~1.6-1.9 for Adv 7000-15000. The ratio falls with rank because at the very top Main has a ceiling (dozens tie at 100 percentile, shift normalisation adds noise) while Advanced still separates students. Caveats: (1) spread is huge: the 25th-75th percentile range at Adv ~5000 is roughly 1x-4x, and coaching sources note Main 20-30k students sometimes reach Advanced top 1000; (2) the relation is asymmetric (regression to the mean): starting from a Main rank m, the median Advanced rank is WORSE than m (about 1.5-2x m in the same model), so do not invert the factor to predict an Advanced rank from a Main rank; (3) a pure equal-standing mapping (same number of Advanced-takers ahead of you) would give only ~1.1-1.3x, so 2.0 places IITs where their admitted students' Main ranks typically fall, not a strict equivalence. Treat as low-to-medium confidence; good enough for ordering a motivational ladder.
